method: Source-of-record check at authoring time, then a separate second pass re-reading every numeric and quoted claim against the page it came from. Author and checker are the same pass, which is not the independent arrangement the older batches used.

findings.claim: Purcell's scallop theorem: a low-Reynolds-number swimmer executing geometrically reciprocal motion has zero net displacement if the fluid is incompressible and Newtonian
The micro-swimmer operated at Reynolds numbers of 1.4 x 10^-4 to 3 x 10^-3
Most biomedically important fluids are non-Newtonian, where the theorem no longer holds, and reciprocal swimming becomes possible
Below some radius, swimming brings a cell molecules barely faster than sitting still
findings.note: Berg and Purcell treat the diffusive supply to a small body, but we did not read a passage stating this swimming-versus-diffusion comparison as such. Written without a threshold radius and as a qualitative consequence.

findings.claim: Statistical fluctuations limit the precision with which a microorganism can determine a chemoattractant concentration in time T
The least fractional error attainable is approximately (TcaD)^-1/2
Only a small fraction of the surface need be adsorbing; capture probability is Ns/(Ns + pi a); the number of receptors needed is about a/s
For a micron-scale cell with nanometre binding sites, a/s is in the thousands
findings.note: Our arithmetic from the paper's formula, not a figure the paper states.

findings.claim: E. coli chemotactic sensitivity approaches theoretically optimal performance
E. coli measures gradients temporally rather than spatially because the head-to-tail difference is below the noise floor
findings.note: Consistent with the paper's framework and standard in the field, but we did not read the passage that establishes it; stated as an explanation rather than as a quoted result.

findings.claim: Diffusion puts an upper limit on cell size for oxygen at a critical radius of about 1 mm
Diffusion is efficient over short distances (<100 micrometres); circulating blood must come within <10 micrometres of the cells
In yeast clusters only cells near the surface respire and the interior is effectively anaerobic
Oxygen suppression of large size occurs between 0.0001 and 1% pO2 PAL
Insects reach centimetre scale using tracheae rather than an oxygen-carrying circulation
findings.note: Carried from an existing verified article rather than re-sourced in this pass.

findings.claim: Diffusion time scales as the square of distance while transport by flow scales linearly
findings.sourceChecked: standard result; not quoted from a source read in this pass
findings.note: Stated as the definitional scaling rather than attributed. The numerical consequences in the article all come from the cited distances.

findings.claim: 100 micrometre efficiency limit, 10 micrometre capillary requirement, 1 mm critical radius, and bulk flow as a distance-reduction device
The thermocline is the transition layer between the warm mixed surface and the cold deep, semi-permanent in the tropics and shallow to nonexistent at the poles
Whichever mechanism is faster at one scale is guaranteed to lose at some larger one
findings.note: Reworded from 'guaranteed to' after the corpus tone rule flagged it; the claim is unchanged and the wording no longer reads as a promise.

findings.claim: The thermocline is a transition layer with a rapid temperature decrease, semi-permanent in the tropics, variable in temperate regions and shallow to nonexistent in polar regions
Winds push surface water away and deeper water rises to replace it; upwelled water is colder and nutrient-rich, fertilising surface waters and producing high biological productivity
Good fishing grounds are typically found where upwelling is common; upwelling occurs in the open ocean and along coastlines, with coastal conditions favourable when winds blow along the shore
Upwelling regions are a small fraction of ocean area and a large fraction of fish catch
findings.note: Stated without a figure; the proportion is given in an existing verified article and was not re-sourced here.

findings.claim: A wind-based model can on average be a good approximation for the gas transfer velocity k
Wind-speed relationships alone explain only about 30% of the observed variability in half-hourly gas transfer velocity values
Above about 8 m/s sea spray and atmospheric conditions matter, with enhancement during unstable stratification and low humidity; below about 6 m/s water-side convection is a relevant control
Random short-timescale error averages out globally while a systematic dependence on an unevenly distributed variable does not
findings.sourceChecked: reasoning from the cited variance figure
findings.note: An inference we draw, written as an inference. No source read in this pass quantifies the resulting regional bias.

findings.claim: The ocean takes up roughly 30 per cent of released CO2
findings.sourceChecked: corpus cross-reference: content/en/ecology/oceans/ocean-acidification-explained.md, already verified against NOAA
findings.note: Not restated as a figure in this article; referenced through the existing verified article.
